name: Xylem
description: Xylem makes the pumps, treatment equipment, smart meters and water-quality sensors used to move, treat, measure and use water, plus services that keep that equipment running. It sells to water and wastewater utilities, industrial plants and commercial and residential buildings, through direct sales and a large distributor network. About 58% of revenue is US. Revenue comes from one-time equipment sales, recurring services and replacement parts, smart-metering networks and software, and some equipment rentals (lease revenue about $140M in H1 2026).

gics.note: Conventional filing label: GICS Sector 'Industrials' and Sub-Industry 'Industrial Machinery & Supplies & Components' per Wikipedia 'List of S&P 500 companies' (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_S%26P_500_companies, read 2026-09-30). That list gives only Sector and Sub-Industry. SEC SIC code 3561 (Pumps & Pumping Equipment) per EDGAR.

hq.note: 301 Water Street SE, Washington, DC 20003 (FY2025 10-K cover). Wikipedia S&P 500 list shows White Plains, New York; see conflicts.

businessLines.name: Water Infrastructure
businessLines.how: Utilities and industrial plants buy pumps and treatment systems as capital equipment (direct and indirect channels), then buy replacement parts and service over the long life of the installed base.
businessLines.description: Water and wastewater pumps (Flygt) and treatment equipment (Wedeco UV, Leopold filtration, Wallace & Tiernan disinfection, Ionpure) that move water from source to user and back to the environment; customers are utilities and industrial plants.

businessLines.name: Applied Water
businessLines.how: Equipment sold to distributors and OEMs, who resell to contractors and building owners; volume driven by construction, building maintenance and industrial activity, with replacement demand for installed pumps.
businessLines.description: Pumps, valves, heat exchangers, controls and dispensing equipment for buildings (residential and commercial) and industrial uses, sold mostly through independent distributors.

revenue.note: Revenue by application: Building Solutions $1,037M (56%), Industrial Water $812M (44%) (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1524472/000152447226000012/xyl-20251231.htm)

businessLines.name: Measurement and Control Solutions
businessLines.how: Utilities buy meters and communications network hardware in multi-year deployments, then pay for software, data analytics and managed services; analytical instruments are sold as equipment plus sensors and consumables.
businessLines.description: Smart water, gas and electric meters (Sensus), the FlexNet communications network, software and analytics, and water-quality instruments (YSI, WTW).

revenue.note: Revenue by application: Smart Metering and Other $1,726M (83%), Analytics $360M (17%) (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1524472/000152447226000012/xyl-20251231.htm)

businessLines.name: Water Solutions and Services
businessLines.how: Customers pay for treatment systems (project and capital sales) and for recurring services, rentals and outsourced operations; emergency-response work is billed on demand.
businessLines.description: Tailored services and systems for industrial and municipal customers: preventive maintenance, rapid-response mobile services, outsourced water operations, mobile dewatering rentals, odor and corrosion control and process-water treatment systems.
